unit: Ch 15: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction, Preamble, Extent and Structure of FEMA, 1999
explain: FEMA replaced FERA (1973) and came into effect on 1st June, 2000.
Its main objective is facilitating external trade and payments and promoting the orderly development of the Indian foreign exchange market.
It extends to the whole of India and to all branches, offices, and agencies outside India owned or controlled by a resident in India.
RBI exercises overall management control over foreign exchange transactions.
Enforcement of FEMA provisions is entrusted to the Directorate of Enforcement under Section 36.

flow.title: Evolution and Enforcement Structure of FEMA
steps: Defense of India Rules 1939 introduced
FERA 1947 enacted then replaced by FERA 1973
FEMA 1999 enacted effective 1st June 2000
Applies to whole India and overseas PRII branches
RBI manages forex while Enforcement Directorate enforces law

topics.example: An Indian company's branch office located in London is subject to FEMA because it is owned or controlled by a person resident in India.
remember: FEMA came into force on 1st June 2000.
Enforcement is handled by the Directorate of Enforcement under Section 36.
mistakes: Thinking FEMA only applies within the geographical boundaries of India—it also covers overseas branches owned or controlled by Indian residents.

quiz.q: On which date did the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 come into force?
quiz.why: FEMA 1999 came into force with effect from 1st June, 2000 vide Notification G.S.R. 371(E).

quiz.q: Which authority is entrusted with the enforcement of FEMA provisions under Section 36?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
quiz.why: While RBI handles overall management, enforcement is entrusted to a separate Directorate of Enforcement under Section 36.

topics.title: Key Definitions under FEMA (Authorised Person, Currency & Foreign Exchange)
explain: Authorised Person under Section 2(c) includes an authorised dealer, money changer, off-shore banking unit, or any person authorised under Section 10(1).
Currency under Section 2(h) includes currency notes, postal notes, money orders, cheques, drafts, travelers' cheques, letters of credit, bills of exchange, and credit cards.
Foreign Exchange under Section 2(n) includes foreign currency, deposits/balances payable in foreign currency, and drafts/cheques drawn in Indian currency but payable in foreign currency.
Foreign Security under Section 2(o) means any security denominated or expressed in foreign currency, including securities where returns are payable in Indian currency.
Person under Section 2(u) includes individuals, HUF, companies, firms, AOP/BOI, artificial juridical persons, and any agency or branch owned/controlled by them.

flow.title: Components of Foreign Exchange under Section 2(n)
steps: Foreign Currency Notes and Bank Notes
Deposits and Balances in Foreign Currency
Drafts in INR payable in Foreign Currency
Instruments drawn outside India payable in INR
All combined form Foreign Exchange under Sec 2(n)

topics.example: A traveler's cheque drawn in Indian Rupees but payable in US Dollars abroad qualifies as foreign exchange under Section 2(n).
remember: Authorised Person under Sec 2(c) covers dealers, money changers, and offshore banking units authorized by RBI.
mistakes: Believing credit cards or traveler's cheques are not considered 'currency'—Section 2(h) explicitly includes credit cards and traveler's cheques.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT included in the definition of 'Authorised Person' under Section 2(c)?
quiz.why: Authorised Person includes authorised dealers, money changers, off-shore banking units, or persons authorised under Sec 10(1).

quiz.q: Which of the following items is included in the definition of 'Currency' under Section 2(h)?
quiz.why: Section 2(h) defines currency to include currency notes, cheques, drafts, credit cards, bills of exchange, and promissory notes.

topics.title: Determination of Residential Status under FEMA
explain: A Person Resident in India (PRII) under Section 2(v) is an individual residing in India for more than 182 days during the preceding financial year.
Exception A: A person who leaves India for employment, business/vocation, or an uncertain stay abroad becomes a Person Resident Outside India (PROI) from the date of departure.
Exception B: A person who comes to India otherwise than for employment, business, or uncertain stay remains a PROI even if staying over 182 days.
FEMA residential status is not for a whole year; it applies from a specific date based on intent and purpose.
Corporate bodies registered in India, and Indian offices/branches owned/controlled by PROIs, are legally PRII.

flow.title: Testing Individual Residential Status under FEMA
steps: Check stay in India during preceding financial year
If 182 days or less person is PROI
If more than 182 days check departure purpose
If left for employment status changes to PROI
If came for non-employment visit status remains PROI

topics.example: Mr. A stayed in India for 200 days in FY 2024-25. On 10th May 2025, he moved to the USA to take up a job. He becomes a PROI from 10th May 2025.
remember: 182 days stay in the preceding financial year + purpose of stay/departure determines residential status.
Citizenship is not the criterion under FEMA.
mistakes: Assuming Indian citizenship automatically makes someone a resident—citizenship is irrelevant; physical stay and intention determine status.

quiz.q: Mr. X resided in India for 210 days in FY 2024-25. On 1st June 2025, he left India to take up permanent employment in London. What is his residential status from 1st June 2025?
o: Person Resident in India for whole FY 2025-26
Person Resident Outside India from 1st June 2025
Person Resident in India till 31st March 2026
Non-resident only if he acquires foreign citizenship
quiz.why: Under Section 2(v)(A), a person who leaves India for employment outside India becomes a PROI from the date of departure.

quiz.q: Which of the following entities is automatically considered a 'Person Resident in India' under FEMA?
o: A company incorporated in Japan with no office in India
A branch office in Mumbai owned by a foreign company
An Indian citizen living in the UK for 10 years working there
A foreign student studying in India for a 3-month course
quiz.why: Section 2(v)(iii) specifies that an office, branch or agency in India owned or controlled by a person resident outside India is a PRII.

topics.title: Regulation and Management of Foreign Exchange
explain: Section 3 prohibits dealing in or transferring foreign exchange/security except through an Authorised Person (AP).
Section 3(b) & (c) bar making payments to or receiving payments on behalf of a Person Resident Outside India without AP or RBI permission.
Section 3(d) prohibits entering into financial transactions in India (like Hawala) as consideration for acquiring assets outside India.
Section 4 mandates that no PRII shall acquire, hold, own, possess, or transfer foreign exchange, foreign security, or overseas immovable property except as permitted under the Act.

flow.title: Restrictions on Foreign Exchange Transactions
steps: Identify proposed transaction involving foreign exchange
Check if transaction is routed through Authorised Person
Verify no prohibited Hawala arrangement exists
Ensure compliance with Section 3 and Section 4
Execute transaction legally through authorized channels

topics.example: A tourist offering US Dollar cash directly to a local restaurant in India is prohibited; the restaurant must hold a money changer license to accept foreign currency.
remember: Section 3 bans unauthorized forex dealing and Hawala transactions.
Section 4 restricts holding foreign exchange or foreign property without permission.
mistakes: Believing a resident can freely hold onto foreign currency received as a gift abroad without bringing it back under repatriation rules.

quiz.q: Under Section 3 of FEMA, an Indian resident paying cash in INR to a local dealer in exchange for foreign currency delivered to his relative abroad is engaging in an illegal transaction commonly known as:
quiz.why: Section 3(d) prohibits financial transactions in India linked to asset acquisition or payment creation outside India, covering Hawala.

quiz.q: According to Section 4 of FEMA 1999, which of the following actions by a resident in India is restricted unless permitted under the Act?
quiz.why: Section 4 restricts acquiring, holding, owning, possessing, or transferring foreign exchange, foreign security, or foreign immovable property.

topics.title: Current Account Transactions & Rules
topics.section: Section 5 & CAT Rules, 2000 (Schedules I, II, III)
explain: Current Account Transactions under Section 2(j) are transactions other than capital account transactions, including trade payments, interest/net income, living expenses, and travel/education/medical costs.
Current account transactions are freely permitted unless specifically restricted under FEM (Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000.
Schedule I lists prohibited transactions (e.g., lottery winnings, racing/riding income, sweepstakes, call-back services).
Schedule II lists transactions requiring prior approval of the Central Government (e.g., cultural tours, foreign print media ads > USD 10,000 by State Govt/PSU, transponder hiring).
Schedule III lists transactions requiring RBI approval / limits (LRS limit for individuals is USD 250,000 per FY; corporate consultancy limits USD 10M for infrastructure / USD 1M for others).

flow.title: Classification of Current Account Transactions
steps: Check if transaction alters overseas assets or liabilities
If no it is a Current Account Transaction
Check Schedule I: If listed drawal is prohibited
Check Schedule II: If listed Government approval needed
Check Schedule III: If exceeding limit RBI approval needed

topics.example: Remitting US$ 50,000 out of lottery winnings abroad is strictly prohibited under Schedule I of the CAT Rules.
remember: LRS limit for individuals is USD 250,000 per financial year for permissible current/capital account transactions.
mistakes: Confusing Schedule II (Government approval) with Schedule III (RBI approval). Cultural tours require Ministry approval, whereas standard medical/education abroad falls under LRS limits.

quiz.q: Which of the following current account transactions is strictly PROHIBITED under Schedule I of the CAT Rules, 2000?
quiz.why: Schedule I explicitly prohibits drawal of foreign exchange for remittance out of lottery winnings.

quiz.q: Under Schedule III of CAT Rules 2000, what is the maximum Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) limit per financial year for an individual without prior RBI approval?
quiz.why: Individuals can avail of foreign exchange facility up to USD 250,000 per financial year under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme.

topics.title: Capital Account Transactions & Provisions
explain: Capital Account Transaction under Section 2(e) is a transaction that alters assets or liabilities (including contingent liabilities) outside India of PRII, or in India of PROI.
General rule: Capital account transactions are prohibited unless specifically permitted by RBI or Central Government regulations.
Prohibited capital investments for PROI in India: Chit fund business, Nidhi company, Agricultural/plantation activities, Real estate business (excluding township/construction/REITs), and TDR trading.
Section 6(4) allows a PRII to hold, own, transfer or invest in foreign currency/security/property if acquired when resident outside India or inherited from a PROI.
Section 6(5) allows a PROI to hold, own, transfer or invest in Indian currency/security/property if acquired when resident in India or inherited from a PRII.

flow.title: Capital Account Transaction Permissibility Check
steps: Identify if transaction alters cross-border assets or liabilities
Check if prohibited like Chit funds or Nidhi
Check if general or specific permission exists
Verify Sec 6(4) or 6(5) pre-existing asset exemption
If permitted proceed within prescribed limits

topics.example: A Non-Resident Indian (NRI) cannot invest in an Indian partnership firm engaged in real estate business or purchasing agricultural land.
remember: Sec 6(4) protects foreign assets acquired by a PRII while living abroad.
Sec 6(5) protects Indian assets acquired by a PROI while living in India.
mistakes: Assuming 'Real Estate Business' under FEMA prohibits township development or REITs—construction of residential/commercial premises and REITs are explicitly excluded from the prohibition.

quiz.q: Which of the following business sectors is strictly PROHIBITED for investment by a Person Resident Outside India (PROI) under FEMA capital account regulations?
quiz.why: PROIs are prohibited from investing in Chit funds, Nidhi companies, agricultural/plantation activities, real estate business, and TDR trading.

quiz.q: Under Section 6(4) of FEMA, an Indian resident who previously lived abroad MAY hold foreign currency or property abroad IF:
o: He pays a 30% tax penalty to RBI
It was acquired when he was resident outside India
He converts it into INR within 30 days
He gets annual permission from the Ministry of External Affairs
quiz.why: Section 6(4) permits a PRII to hold/own foreign currency, securities, or property acquired when he was a PROI or inherited from a PROI.
